transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net billing customer care, my name is Zack. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Zack. I am looking at my online banking app right now and S-Net has taken two separate direct debits today, one for fifty-seven pounds and another for fifty-seven pounds! You've charged me twice for my broadband upgrade!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how alarming it is to see two identical debits deducted on the same day, Elizabeth. Let me inspect your billing account immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Zack, because fifty-seven pounds coming out twice has pushed my current account into unauthorized overdraft.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I access the billing ledger, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the address is 22 Priory Crescent, Lewes, BN7 1HP, and my security PIN is 5912.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Elizabeth. Can you confirm the primary account holder name and your registered contact telephone number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The account is under Elizabeth Turner, and my mobile is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero eight one four. Both debits came out this morning on Tuesday the 14th of October.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Elizabeth, I have pulled up your master billing profile and subscription ledger on our billing console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I upgraded our package from Superfast 100 to Gigafast 900 at the beginning of this month after seeing your promotional flyer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the upgrade work order was successfully provisioned on the first of October by our provisioning team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The sales representative assured me that the first monthly invoice on the new tariff wouldn't be deducted until our regular November billing run.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When broadband packages are upgraded mid-cycle, our billing platform automatically calculates prorated charges for the remaining days of the old tier alongside advance billing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Prorated charges make sense, but why on earth would there be two separate deductions of the exact same fifty-seven pound amount taken simultaneously?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me examine the invoice breakdown and ledger journal entries for both billing transactions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The bank statement lists two identical references: S-NET-INV-77102 and S-NET-INV-77103, both for fifty-seven pounds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Were both payments deducted from your primary current account ending in 4108 with NatWest Bank?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, both transactions were debited from that exact NatWest current account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did your bank notify you that the unexpected duplicate transaction triggered an unarranged overdraft fee or penalty charge?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my NatWest banking app immediately flagged an unarranged overdraft penalty fee of fifteen pounds because my balance dropped below zero.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will ensure that any banking penalty charges resulting from our billing error are fully reimbursed as account credits, Elizabeth.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is reassuring to hear, Zack, because that overdraft fee was caused entirely by S-Net taking double money.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking into invoice 77102, that was generated as a final balancing reconciliation invoice for the Superfast 100 package.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why would a balancing invoice on a thirty-eight pound contract come out as fifty-seven pounds?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The automated billing system erroneously applied the new Gigafast monthly tariff rate of fifty-seven pounds to the final balancing period instead of thirty-eight pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And then invoice 77103 billed another fifty-seven pounds for the advance month of October to November?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely. The billing engine failed to merge the migration credit before submitting the automated BACS payment collection tape to the clearing house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So your automated computer system basically charged me for two full months of Gigafast on the exact same morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that is an accurate assessment of how the dual BACS transmission occurred.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does your billing system not have automated validation thresholds that flag duplicate identical debits before transmission?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Normally our automated audit script flags duplicate amounts within forty-eight hours, but mid-contract tariff migrations bypass that filter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like a massive flaw in the upgrade ordering pipeline.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged a technical ticket with our IT billing infrastructure team to patch that migration script exception.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you reverse that duplicate fifty-seven pounds back into my NatWest bank account immediately?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about thirty-five seconds while I liaise with our senior billing reconciliation department to review the duplicate ledger entries.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Elizabeth. The billing reconciliation team has confirmed the duplicate collection error on invoice 77103.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So how quickly does that fifty-seven pounds get returned into my bank account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under standard direct debit scheme operating procedures, duplicate payments are settled by applying an account credit of fifty-seven pounds against your next scheduled invoice in November.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, are you telling me you won't refund the cash into my bank account right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Company billing guidelines dictate that overpayments under seventy-five pounds are automatically absorbed as forward billing credits on the following monthly statement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why would your policy force an account credit when the duplicate charge was completely S-Net's fault?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The automated BACS reconciliation gateway consolidates monthly balances automatically at each billing cycle cutoff.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you not speak to a billing duty manager to issue an immediate cash clawback to my bank today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Even supervisory staff must adhere to standard banking indemnification turnaround windows unless an emergency exception is granted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you serious?! That is completely unacceptable! You took money out of my account that I need for my mortgage payment today! How on earth can you expect me to wait four weeks for an account credit when your system made the mistake?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Direct debit reversal procedures require fourteen working days under standard banking rules, so account credits are our default mechanism.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I cannot wait fourteen working days when my Nationwide mortgage payment bounces tomorrow morning! This is utterly disgraceful customer service!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand your urgency, Elizabeth. I have the supervisory authority to submit an emergency manual faster payment refund request.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long will an emergency manual faster payment take to actually reach my NatWest account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An emergency faster payment clears directly into your current account within twenty-four to forty-eight hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Forty-eight hours is significantly better than waiting four weeks, although I still need to borrow money from my sister to cover the mortgage tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also apply a fifteen-pound credit to cover your overdraft fee and an additional twenty-pound goodwill credit for the stress caused.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The goodwill credit helps compensate for the severe stress and panic this caused me this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you remind me what date the unauthorized direct debit was taken from your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you right at the start of our call, Tuesday the 14th of October.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Elizabeth. I am entering Tuesday the 14th of October into the manual BACS faster payment authorization form right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the manual refund go directly into account 4108?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it transmits directly to sort code 60-12-34, account 4108 via the UK Faster Payments electronic banking network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will I receive an email confirmation once the finance team executes the transfer so I have written documentary proof for NatWest?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, an automated remittance advice notice will be emailed to your registered address at e.turner@example.co.uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is the actual Gigafast 900 broadband performance working for you since the physical installation?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The internet speed itself has been fantastic, we're getting nine hundred megabytes download, so the service is great.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am delighted to hear that. The refund reference is REF-88192-FP. I have confirmed thirty-five pounds credit and the faster payment. Does that fully resolve your billing inquiry today, Elizabeth?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, Zack, you've sorted out the refund and the credits. Thank you for your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Elizabeth. Have a wonderful rest of your day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Zack, goodbye.
